sentences.text: Andrew Johnson was driving the train that made an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon The driver of a high-speed train where a mass stabbing took place said he had "probably about 10 seconds" to decide to switch to the slow line before making an unscheduled stop.

sentences.article_title: Train attack driver's '10 seconds' to change line

sentences.text: The next census should include more ethnicity options to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English, according to a group of MPs.

sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: At the 2021 census, the ethnic group section saw English offered only within the white category.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: He said: "But my parents and I were born in England, we grew up in England, our home is in England, yet some voices attempt to reduce Englishness to a skin colour and to a bloodline.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: "Well, if we're going to go down that path, my mum's side of the family has been English for as far back as we have traced." The Eastbourne MP said he had received "death threats for daring to say that you don't have to be white to be English".
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: He added "English ethnicity is real" before arguing it is a "matter of historical fact that it has never been one bloodline" and "even our Royal Family has German roots".
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: "Is the King not English either, I ask." Addressing the ethnicity section of the census, Babarinde said the "only box that says English sits under the white category".
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: He added: "If you are black, the form offers you black British, if you are Asian, it offers you Asian British, but not English.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: "Now, the same question in the Welsh census offers a black Welsh category.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: In Scotland, the census offers Scottish Asian, for example.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: "Yet the best that England offers in our census is a miscellaneous write-in box that may as well be the margin." Lammy, a former deputy prime minister, said in a statement: "It is quite absurd that neither I or my mixed heritage children can describe themselves as black or mixed race and English on our census form.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: "I have long campaigned for us to change to the position enjoyed by others in Wales and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: We have to end this backward racial gatekeeping." Babarinde told the BBC he had brought forward the PMB because there were "some corners of our politics who are attempting to gatekeep Englishness for people who are a particular colour".
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: He also said there are "people like Suella Braverman who have really undermined and questioned the Englishness of people like me".
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: In 2025, Braverman - then a Conservative MP before her defection to Reform UK - wrote in the Daily Telegraph , external that she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: In recent weeks, Braverman has reaffirmed her position and wrote on X , external : "To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity.

sentences.text: It also denies me my Asian heritage." She also said "Englishness is an ethnicity", adding: "There have been English people for centuries and we need to recognise this more if we are to start taking a more muscular approach to citizenship and nationality.
sentences.article_title: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

sentences.text: And no, it's not racist to say this." Babarinde introduced his PMB to the Commons using the 10-minute rule process.

sentences.text: Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But head teachers' unions said schools would struggle to implement stricter new policies without additional funding from government.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government's "clear message" to parents and pupils was that "school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But he said the more robust measures recommended under the new guidance would "come at a cost".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said the latest guidance "does at least provide some clarity", but added that school leaders "cannot simply make mobile phones disappear".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "If all schools are going to be expected to have lockable pouches or other secure storage facilities for every pupil, the cost involved will be very significant indeed," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "This is not feasible unless the government puts in the funding required to meet these costs." Responding to questions about funding, Powell told BBC Breakfast that she wanted heads to have the autonomy to implement the policies that work best for their schools.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, said she welcomed strong action to stop phones distracting pupils and disrupting the school day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Charlotte Ashton, co-founder of campaign group of Generation Focus, similarly welcomed the changes, saying "no see, no hear" policies were not working and pupils were still "TikToking in the toilets".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we need to get to a point where it's not normal for every single child to have a personal internet-enabled device in their pockets with them 24/7," she said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: A smartphone ban in English schools is coming into force.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Parents want to ban smartphones in schools, but there's one reason they're worried Shadow Education Secretary Laura Trott said she was "delighted that Labour have finally listened to us and agreed to properly ban smartphones in schools".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: She said it was also the "right thing to do" to have a review of safety standards around the technology used in schools, which the government has also announced on the back of calls for improved guidance .
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But she criticised what she called a lack of "joined up thinking" over what new tech was being allowed in classrooms.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Because education is devolved, the approach to phones in schools varies across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: In Scotland , external , the government has said it will introduce a new law to restrict the personal use of phones in schools, and launched a consultation on the issue over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: In Wales , external , the Senedd recently voted against a motion to introduce a national statutory ban on phones in classrooms.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: The Welsh government launched a 12-week consultation in September, which it says will shape its guidance to support schools in developing a mobile phone policy.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools are still encouraged to restrict the use of phones during the school day, but heads have flexibility over how to implement their own rules.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: And in Northern Ireland , Education Minister Paul Givan launched a 12-week consultation in August on whether to ban mobile phones from schools by law, calling for "a stronger and more consistent approach across our education system".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Rules around phones in schools are separate from the UK's upcoming ban on social media for under-16s, due to be introduced in March.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Children will be barred from accessing platforms like Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Vinted and eBay could also be included in the list of platforms set to be banned, the culture secretary has said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Taylor Lee died in Plymouth in November 2023 A school's strict rules contributed to the suicide of a 15-year-old boy and there is a risk of future deaths, a coroner had concluded.
sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: An inquest at Exeter Coroner's Court heard Taylor Lee, a pupil at Ivybridge Community College, Devon, part of Westcountry Schools Trust, took his own life in November 2023.
sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: Area coroner Alison Longhorn ruled the cause of Lee's death was suicide, but also concluded he struggled with what he perceived as unfair school sanctions.
sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: Longhorn is preparing a rare Prevention of Future Deaths report.

sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: Lee, from Plymouth, died weeks after he complained publicly about the school's introduction of stricter rules about being on time for lessons.
sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: Ivybridge Community College uses a system of what it described as "reset" and "reflection" - by which pupils are separated from their classmates for part or the whole of the school day.
sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.article_title: School's strict rules led to boy's death - inquest

sentences.text: The government launched a review into its policy to ban new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035 The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Downing Street has insisted no decision has been made.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The key meetings on the subject will instead be chaired by Cabinet Office minister Louise Haigh.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point." Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Last month, it said , external reducing targets could damage "the investment certainty needed to deliver the infrastructure, innovation and services required for the transition to zero-emission transport".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Asked if climate change was no longer a big priority, Health Minister Karin Smyth said the government was committed to its emissions targets.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: "This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables – that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Last week, head of the association Mike Hawes said transitioning to electric vehicles had come at a "heavy cost" with billions spent on discounts to drive demand in electric vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: He said the government's targets could not be achieved "without putting at risk any future investment".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The government's policy to phase out petrol and diesel vehicle sales has undergone multiple changes since it was first introduced by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: His successor Rishi Sunak pushed back the timeline to 2035, and the Burnham government set up a review of the EV sales targets in August.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Sunak introduced phased targets for EV sales in the UK, known as the Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV) mandate.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The target was 28% for 2025, 33% for 2026, and so on until it reaches 80% by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The Conservative Party has also vowed to abandon the petrol car ban if it wins the next election, with leader Kemi Badenoch calling it a "well-meaning, but ultimately destructive piece of legislation".

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It is a true engineering marvel.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Engine-makers continually vie for access to the technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Rolls-Royce, GE and France's Safran are among the few firms that have perfected the process.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: In September, GE Aerospace announced , external it would acquire its turbine blade supplier for $11.75bn (£8.78bn).
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Neither company responded to BBC News' requests for comment but the move has been described as an effort to ensure supply of these critical components.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Separately, in March, Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham blade casting facility.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Turbine blade specialists continue to work on improving the capabilities of this little-known technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: All the while, China is desperate to prove that its engineers can produce turbine blades of the same quality as those in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Who will come out on top?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Demand for [turbine blades] is huge.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: So few companies have managed to do it, which does give it this kind of magical aura," says Bill Sweetman, an aviation industry writer and consultant.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: He suspects GE Aerospace's recent move is about securing reliability and predictability in the notoriously volatile aircraft manufacturing supply chain.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The casts play a crucial part in the cooling process But why is the single crystal casting process, which has been around for decades now, still so specialist?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: To grow one of these blades, asserts Fifoot, is to "fight the laws of the universe".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: This is because each molten blade would naturally cool into a solid object consisting of many small grains of metal alloy, all jumbled together.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But you don't want a crumbly sugar cube, you want a perfect diamond.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Getting a single crystal to grow into the shape of the blade instead isn't just a matter of cooling the molten version down slowly, the process also uses a bizarre trick called a pigtail.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Sometimes a blade doesn't cool quite as planned, for example two crystals form within it instead of just one, and the metal alloy must be reprocessed so that the manufacturer may re-use the material.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Special ceramic coatings also protect blades from extreme temperatures inside engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And another important feature is that blades are cast with tiny channels that allow a flow of cooler air to coat them in a kind of film while the aircraft engine is working.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "The drive at the moment [across the industry] is currently to make those cooling passages really intricate," says Paul Withey, at the University of Birmingham, who formerly worked for Rolls-Royce.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The more turbulent those little flows of cool air are, he explains, the more they will knock heat out of the surrounding, much hotter air.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And blade-makers also seek to reduce the mass of these components as much as possible.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "If we can take any weight out of it, you can run that engine more efficiently using less fuel – you can spin it faster and hotter," says Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The turbine blades are used in the Trent 1000 engine among others Meanwhile, China hopes to become only the sixth country to master the whole technology chain for single crystal blade casting.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A report in May , external quoted one engineer at the AECC Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials claiming that China now had a single crystal alloy "superior to or equivalent to the second-generation single-crystal superalloys widely used in Europe and the US".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It costs less to make, too, apparently.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But the West has a "huge advantage" over China given that the majority of commercial airliner production happens there, says Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Supply chains and the latest innovations are generally clustered in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Plus, Western manufacturers also have lengthy safety records under their belts.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: China must compete on practically every aspect of aircraft manufacturing , external – by no means just on turbine blades – in order to make serious in-roads.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "You can definitely see that happening but it's a long, uphill struggle," adds Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Demand for aircraft is currently high, which is already straining various supply chains in the industry.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: That demand could grow higher still, suggests Withey.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the next few years, one of the two main aircraft manufacturers, Airbus and Boeing, could launch a new short-haul plane , external , he says.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Then, the other would have to follow suit in order to remain competitive.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "There'll be a bun fight," says Withey, over who gets to supply the engines and, by extension, those all-important single crystal turbine blades. sentences.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is often rated as one of the greatest video games The moment she saw footage from the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kacey Doran picked up her phone.

sentences.text: She had to tell her sister.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: "Have you seen this?" messaged Doran, excitedly.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons.
sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Doran's sister messaged back: "I'm not tearing up… YOU'RE tearing up." News of a video game remake bought back happy memories for Kacey Doran This is the power of nostalgia – and a perfect example of how video games can trigger it.

sentences.text: The country has a word, "yuurei", which means a lingering, troubled spirit.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: These are the ghosts of people who died in violent or tragic circumstances - those who were murdered, killed themselves, or simply were lonely and died alone.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: If they died at home, then the belief is that their yuurei won't go away.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: For house hunters who are not superstitious or squeamish it means there are big bargains to be found.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: There is a whole category of dwellings called jiko bukken, which means "stigmatised" or "incident" properties.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Under guidelines issued by the government in 2021, Japanese estate agents must disclose suicide, murder, death by fire, and any death where the body was not discovered for an extended period of time.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: For rental properties this information must be disclosed for three years, and it must be revealed indefinitely for any property offered for sale.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: By contrast, in the UK there is no legal requirement to reveal that a person died in a property.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: And in the US, it differs from state to state. , external For example, in California you have to reveal if a person has died in the property in the past three years, while in Arizona and Oregon you do not.

sentences.text: "The worst thing is if a suicide has happened in the apartment.
sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.article_title: 'I live with a ghost' - inside the haunted homes attracting bargain hunters

sentences.text: Other issues are a serious crime or a lonely death." The latter issue, that of a person dying alone, would not generally affect the price of a property in, say, the UK or the US.

sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood says she'd like to still pick up the traditional PR skills her role isn't currently focused on, but is confident of her future in the agency's growing AI team.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There's certain things that I haven't had the chance to do yet, like directly pitching to the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: I absolutely plan to do this," she says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Graduates becoming too AI-centric is an issue for Simon Pratt, chief operating officer at Portman Finance Group.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He says being able to use AI effectively is important, but the company's two-year graduate programme is fully centred on "learning the trade".
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Our graduates rotate across four areas at six-month intervals, working directly alongside senior relationship managers to learn their trade," Northampton-based Pratt explains.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "They'll learn all of our financial products, how to draft credit papers for submission to lenders, and how to build meaningful relationships with our customers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: They'll progress to running transactions from start to finish." Claire Reid, PwC UK's chief technology and innovation officer, believes graduate roles that are too AI heavy won't necessarily provide graduates long-term career progression.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There will be no graduate job now that doesn't require a baseline of AI literacy," says Glasgow-based Reid.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "But AI skills on their own are not going to help you in your career.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: You've got to couple that with that sector knowledge of what that client actually wants." Back in Coventry, Dillan Patel is confident his AI work will continue to be valuable, and he wants to keep building on it.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I don't think I'd want to explore different positions within the business.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Through my involvement in AI-related projects, I already work closely with different areas of the business and I'm gaining valuable knowledge and experience along the way," he says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: She's also given up on cycling to the local parks where she previously enjoyed taking close-up photos of the bugs, lizards and toads.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It's all because she can't stand the sound of the delivery drones that fly overhead, depositing her neighbours' online orders.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It triggers my fight or flight response," says the 44-year-old administrative assistant.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "You can hear the drones on approach and you can hear them inside your home when they pass directly overhead and then you hear them as they leave," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Smaller drone delivery services are popping up too: in some US cities, customers can order flying treats from their local pizza joint or ice cream parlour.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: People who benefit from a drone delivery service, for example, may be less bothered by the noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The FAA says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for addressing any community concerns.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets encloses some of the blades on its drone inside a pod Might better technology muffle the irritating buzz?
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: One startup, Greenjets, set out to tackle both "noise level and the frequency of that noise," as Darren James, future technologies lead at the company, puts it.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The London-based business has designed a propulsion system it claims can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While standard drones use spinning propellers that slice through open air, creating that high-pitched buzz, Greenjets encloses spinning blades inside a pod, to muffle the sound and direct the noise away from the ground.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Its system also quietens things down through slower rotor speed and by using materials that reduce vibration noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Making quieter drones isn't just about keeping the noise down for neighbours who are already sick of airborne deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets' low-noise tech has been used by police and harbour security teams in Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also helped conservationists in Africa, who are seeking to track poachers from above without being detected.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Battlefield drone operators also have good reason to keep the noise down, to avoid alerting the enemy of the approach of their unmanned vehicles.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "There are some efforts to reduce the sound of drones.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The US Special Forces are interested, at an experimental stage," says Robert Tollast, a research fellow at Whitehall think tank The Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: But he stresses that drone speed, rather than stealthiness, tends to come first for larger drones used in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "Make it faster, not less quiet, seems to be the approach," says Tollast.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – except that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Specifically, it was the tips of the blades that he realised were creating the noise as they swiped through the air.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I asked myself a very simple question, what would a tipless propeller look like and how would it function?" The result was to create a propeller with twisted loop-shaped blades with no points.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It turned out it was easier to test his propeller in water than it was to repeatedly fly a drone, which led Sharrow to initially develop a less noisy boat propeller.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Now, however, his company, Sharrow Engineering, is focusing on developing "ultra-quiet" drone rotors.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "We have validated that the technology works in drone applications and that it is dramatically quieter," says Sharrow.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Companies at the forefront of drone deliveries say they are also working to reduce the noise of their fleets.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Amazon says it has made "measurable sound improvements" to its drones and its latest designs use custom-designed propellers "that produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation, with a milder tone".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Drone maker Wing, which provides its vehicles for Walmart deliveries, says its propellers are designed to minimise noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It also varies its flight paths to prevent repeated overflights over any single home or neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: For Schmidt, fed up with the noise of drones, the only truly satisfactory solution would be to halt drone deliveries in her area.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I would like them to completely stop until they figure out how their services stop being a nuisance," she says.

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She says that would "catch" more people with low vitamin D and give a more accurate picture of how widespread the issue is.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday warns of "a lifelong deficit" in women - in adolescence, then pregnancy, and then the newborn is affected.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: He tells me that despite being 100 years on from the discovery of vitamin D "rickets hasn't gone away".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If we have rickets in the community, there are going to be many more people who are vitamin D deficient." He says the government should look into wider fortification of food in which vitamins are added to foods during production.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Countries like Canada and Sweden have mandatory policies.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, some foods such as breakfast cereals and spreads are already fortified with vitamin D, but it is voluntary.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: During the winter months, people start to lose their vitamin D levels.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "We might have to accept that for certain groups vitamin D supplementation is a matter of course," says Hewison.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia is now taking vitamin D supplements regularly - and is back in goal.

sentences.text: Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But many earn tens of thousands in extra payments and awards.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Stockpiles of blood have dropped below required levels due to falling donor numbers An amber alert has come into force for the first time as stocks of blood in Scotland have dropped to unprecedented low levels due to the shortage of donors.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The warning has been sent to hospitals across the country by the Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service (SNBTS), urging medical staff to only use Type O blood when essential.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: Type O blood is particularly important for transfusions as O-negative acts as a universal donor and O-positive is the most common blood type in the UK, with about 35% of the population having it.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: Stocks have consistently been below target levels for several weeks and Group O blood has fallen to below two days of reserves on several occasions recently.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: SNBTS aims to always retain 5 – 7 days supply of all blood groups.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The alert comes after a decline in people joining the blood donation register.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: In the past decade SNBTS said there had been a 24% drop in blood donors - about  30,000 people.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The blood transfusion service said it was particularly struggling to attract younger donors.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: Hospitals are estimated to need about 135,000 units of blood each year to treat patients.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The SNBTS said that to do this appointments at its five national donor centres in Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Inverness needed to be fully booked all year round.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: However, an average of just 85% of these appointment slots are filled.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: Debbie McNaughton, director of donor and transport services at the SNBTS, told Radio Scotland Breakfast that currently, about 2% of Scotland's population are signed up to give blood, with the majority donating once a year.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: "If they could be donating maybe twice or three times a year, that would hugely help to provide resilience for the blood supply," she said.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: McNaughton went on to urge anyone who is healthy and 17 or over to sign up to the donor register.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The amber alert will trigger new protocols in hospitals to minimise non-essential usage of O-type blood, but emergency operations, blood transfusions, transplants and cancer surgeries will continue as normal.
sentences.article_title: Amber alert as Scotland faces blood donation shortages

sentences.text: The alert has initially been issued for an initial period of 4-6 weeks but will be kept under close review.

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
