sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.

sentences.text: Ofcom has set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Under the UK's social media ban - which is due to come into force in March next year - those under that age will be prevented from accessing ten of the biggest platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: The UK says it intends to take a tougher approach.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Age verification below 18 is challenging because 16 and 17 year olds don't have credit cards or full driving licences, and may not have passports either.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: They can also look significantly older or younger than they are.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However, ultimately it will be up to the tech companies to figure out how to implement the checks: the onus is on social network providers to come up with their own solutions and comply.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Meta told the BBC it already applies some methods recommended by Ofcom to enforce its user age requirements or place users in Teen Accounts settings.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But it said applying age checks at device-level, via app stores, could reduce the burden on people to have to repeatedly verify their age across multiple platforms.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: This would place responsibility with Apple and Google, who between them operate most of the world's smartphones.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Apple has already introduced age verification in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However Ofcom says that would not absolve the social network providers from doing their own checks as well.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Dawes said making the ban work would be a joint effort.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "At Ofcom, what we will do is make sure that the services that the social media companies put in the checks that they need to," she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's our job, but the wider question about how everybody engages with this, it is for everybody, really.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Child safety campaigners including the Molly Rose Foundation and NSPCC welcomed Ofcom's guidance.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But both said there were lessons to be learned from how Australia's social media ban had been implemented, after it was found many under-16s could still access social platforms .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's why, as we prepare to embark on our own social media ban in the UK, we need to make sure we accurately know the age of child users," said Rani Govender, head of child safety online at the NSPCC.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: She said the government and Ofcom must ensure tech firms are held accountable for meeting age check standards "to help keep children safe online and ensure the ban delivers change in practice".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But Andy Burrows, the Molly Rose Foundation's chief executive, said Ofcom had shown a "dire track record" of enforcing the Online Safety Act - raising questions over how effectively it would help deliver a social media ban.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Andy Burnham must deliver a ban that learns the lessons from Australia and that incentivises safety-by-design as the price of admission to the UK market, with a ban as the starting point in a proper plan to give children a safe and happy online life," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Jonny Bunt, corporate affairs director of BT's consumer division, said families should "prepare children for life online after the ban and highlight the risks of trying to dodge the restrictions".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Having those conversations now and giving young people time to prepare for the changes in March will be crucial in helping them adapt to a significant change for a whole generation," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Swans and ducks have enjoyed the wetland reserve at Slimbridge for 80 years Most people know rainforests are vital in the fight against climate change, but now scientists say wetlands could be even more important.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Saltmarshes, mangrove swamps and wetlands can absorb carbon "four times faster than trees", according to the charity the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT).
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Celebrating 80 years since WWT's first wetland bird reserve was founded at Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, the charity's leaders have called for one million hectares of wetlands to be restored across the world.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sarah Fowler, CEO of WWT, said: "They are mood-boosting, flood-buffering, water-purifying, incredible habitats.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But we have lost 85% of the world's wetlands." Sir Peter Scott feeds migrating swans and geese at Slimbridge in 1947, with Desmond Hawkins, BBC features producer from Bristol WWT now runs 10 wetland bird reserves across the UK.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Many people come to enjoy the swans, geese, flamingoes and migrating wildfowl, but do not realise how powerful these habitats can be in soaking up carbon and slowing down climate change.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: So how vital are wetlands for birds, and how powerful can they be in the fight against climate change?
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: This video can not be played The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change In November 1946, a naturalist called Peter Scott came to a wild marshy area on the banks of the River Severn, near Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He was drawn by the thousands of migrating geese and swans that flew thousands of miles from the Russian Arctic to spend the winter here on the mudflats and marshes.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Captivated, Scott settled in a small cottage and later built a house right on a lake, with a huge window to watch the wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He dug lakes and connecting channels, built hides and even towers to watch the birds without disturbing them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the years, the reserve grew and became home to thousands of ducks, swans , geese as well as the migrating wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sir Peter Scott with the first nine Nēnē geese he hand-reared at Slimbridge in 1952 "He really was a pioneer in conservation," said Chris Moore, a historian of Slimbridge and author of Peter Scott and the Birth of Modern Conservation.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: As well as creating a safe haven for endangered species, Scott was a vigorous campaigner for nature.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He led the fight to stop commercial whaling, presented some of the BBC's first natural history programmes called live from Slimbridge, and helped set up WWF, the World Wildlife Fund.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: In 1973 Sir Peter Scott became the first person to be knighted for conservation work.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Moore explained: "Scott was talking about the impact that man was having on the natural world, long before we started talking about climate change and global warming.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "David Attenborough called him the Patron Saint of Conservation, and I think that is more than deserved," Moore added.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Electrical items caused fatal fire, inquest hears Councillor admits harassing bar owner Residents protest against plans for  greenbelt homes One of Scott's typically ambitious projects was to save the Hawaiian Goose, or Nēnē.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Unique to the Pacific islands, the Nēnē was hit hard by road building and development.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: By 1949 barely 24 birds remained.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Scott heard of its plight, and asked Hawaiian authorities to send a few geese to Slimbridge where he hand-reared them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Unfortunately they sent us two females," chuckled Enid Cole, a WWT volunteer at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Peter asked them for a gander - 'It would help', he said." Nine chicks were later born, and hand-raised successfully to adulthood at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Dave Harvey helped to feed the Nēnē geese at Slimbridge Today there are more than 3,000 Nēnē geese, most of them living peacefully on Hawaiian golf courses.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But a handful still live at Slimbridge, where Enid Cole and her friends hand feed them lettuce every day.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "It's a marvelous project, and typical of Sir Peter," Enid smiled.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the last 80 years, the teams at Slimbridge have hand-reared several other species, including the Common Crane and the world's rarest diving duck, the Madagascan Pochard.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: It was while they were working to save the Madagascan Pochard that they realised how vital the wetland habitats were.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "We realised that to save that species, we had to bring the wetland back," explained Sarah Fowler, WWT's chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: And yet, as Fowler explained, "40% of the world's species rely on wetland habitats for survival".
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: What started at Slimbridge has spread to 10 wetland reserves across the UK with the charity now working with local councils to restore wetlands, even in small city areas.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are 'mood-boosting, flood buffering habitats' said Sarah Fowler, Chief Executive of WWT The Wetlands Charity A scheme in Bristol has seen small floating islands of wetland plants moored in the city's harbour.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Across the world, they are campaigning to restore one million hectares of lost wetland, partly to provide safe habitats for endangered species but also because wetlands help absorb carbon far quicker than even forests.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Salt marshes bury carbon," said Fowler.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Every time the big tides go over them, the plants that have grown up in the salt marsh get buried.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Those plants are full of carbon, so they are a massive carbon sink.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "And the brilliant thing about salt marshes is they do this four times faster than trees.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are vital in our fight against climate change, and we must restore them." What started 80 years ago as a bird reserve on the banks of a river in Gloucestershire has grown into a global campaign to restore wetlands, which they call the "soggy secret weapon" against climate change.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The seizure was not connected to Mogambi's individual case.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: If convicted, Mogambi faces a mandatory prison term of at least 10 years, according to the Justice Department.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Authorities say those convicted will also face appropriate orders for forfeiture of assets and restitution to victims, in addition to any prison sentences.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: A world so small that some physicists have nicknamed it the zeptoverse.

sentences.text: The research, led by scientists based in Cambridge, was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).

sentences.text: This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them.

sentences.text: The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.

sentences.text: Many sub-atomic particles are created by smashing the insides of atoms together Dark matter makes up a large part of our cosmos, and yet researchers have struggled to detect it.

sentences.text: Scientists know it is there because its gravitational force influences normal matter, but in all other respects it has remained completely invisible.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: So in this experiment, particles were smashed together at high energy and scientists studied the material that was thrown out - the shrapnel of collisions.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: One of these is a sub-atomic particle - smaller than an atom - called a beauty quark.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Despite its short lifetime, researchers managed to detect it interacting with other tiny particles at a scale of a billion-trillionth of a metre.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Some theories suggest that at these scales particles are more sensitive to dark matter and it could influence how the quarks interact and break down.

sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Net zero means balancing the amount of planet-warming "greenhouse" gases produced by human activities with the amount being actively removed from the atmosphere.

sentences.text: Effectively this means no longer adding to the total amount of these gases in the atmosphere to limit climate change.

sentences.article_title: What is net zero and is the UK on track to achieve it?

sentences.text: In practice, reducing these emissions means switching from coal, oil and gas to cleaner energy sources like wind and solar power.
sentences.article_title: What is net zero and is the UK on track to achieve it?

sentences.text: It also involves adopting green technologies like electric vehicles and heat pumps to replace petrol or diesel cars and gas boilers.
sentences.article_title: What is net zero and is the UK on track to achieve it?

sentences.text: But not all emissions can be eliminated.
sentences.article_title: What is net zero and is the UK on track to achieve it?

sentences.text: M John Harrison was billed by Booker bosses as "a genuinely original thinker" Author M John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, picking up the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: Harrison, 81, who has built a cult following over his 60-year career, was named the winner of the £50,000 prize at a ceremony in London on Monday.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: The End of Everything is set in the years after a mysterious catastrophe that caused British society as we know it to collapse.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: It has divided opinion among readers, and was described as "bleak but brilliant" and "dreamlike and baffling" by one critic.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: He has now surpassed Margaret Atwood as the oldest ever Booker winner.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: While he dislikes labels like science fiction and fantasy, he has been called "the titan of literary science fiction", and Booker Prize chief executive Gaby Wood said he is "the first Booker winner to have emerged from the bona fide SF world".
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: "He is a genuinely original thinker, a genre-defying writer who takes ideas seriously," Wood said.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: "Though very unsettling, The End of Everything is not in fact a strange book.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: The author has said he deliberately omitted as much explanation about the background to the events as possible, in order to make readers feel the same disorientation as the characters.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: He has said: "The End of Everything is about trying to live as if nothing has gone wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'Baffling but brilliant' post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything wins Booker Prize

sentences.text: It's a disaster story in which the disaster is the failure to comprehend." He added: "I've passed on to the reader some of the puzzlement and confusion of the characters in the book as they face a future with the alien." That approach has led to a mixed reaction.

sentences.text: Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa As the sun rises over the Indian Ocean, waves lap onto the golden sands while palm fronds rustle in the cool sea breeze.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: The dunes, she adds, remind some visitors of the Sahara.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: But her tours are about more than scenic views.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She also takes visitors to the fish market, where they discover the variety of marine life available along Somalia's extensive coastline and to parts of the city that reflect its history as a busy Indian Ocean trading centre, with the influences of both its Ottoman and Italian former rulers.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Visitors can also sample Somali food, including camel meat, samosas and traditional tea.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Sucdi says many arrive in the city with expectations shaped by years of hearing about the insecurity.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "Mostly, they are surprised by how beautiful the country is and how welcoming people are," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: At the fish market, she says, visitors are particularly impressed by the variety of fish species.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader wants visitors to experience the "beautiful, welcoming side of Mogadishu" Guiding tours runs in Sucdi's family.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Her father worked in the profession for over three decades, taking journalists, photographers and visitors from different countries around Somalia.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: He introduced her to the business nearly three years ago.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I started this job as a hobby, but it has become something that I like and am passionate about," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She now works alongside her father and a team of guides, building on his experience while using social media to reach a wider audience.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She shares videos of her tours on TikTok, offering people outside Somalia a glimpse of places they may never have imagined visiting.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She is also considering producing content in English to reach audiences who do not speak Somali.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: A wide variety of fish are available in Mogadishu's markets Tourism remains a relatively new field in Somalia, she says, with only a handful working as guides in Mogadishu.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: The business is seasonal, but Sucdi says this year has been particularly encouraging, although numbers are still fairly low.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Having five tourists a week is considered a success but she is confident that numbers will grow.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: However, she says many visitors are still concerned about security.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Since the collapse of Somalia's central government in 1991, Mogadishu has endured decades of civil war, destruction and displacement.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Much of the city centre was reduced to rubble, and basic services and infrastructure largely broke down.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: But following the withdrawal of the Islamist militant group al-Shabab from most of the city in 2011, and the establishment of the federal government in 2012, Mogadishu has undergone a gradual transformation.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Returning members of the Somali diaspora, local entrepreneurs and investors helped fuel a construction boom, with new hotels, restaurants, businesses and residential developments reshaping the capital.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Today, Mogadishu is a growing commercial hub, although insecurity and the legacy of conflict remain part of everyday life.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: About 10,000 tourists visited Somalia in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, according to the country's tourism department.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Many visitors ask about their safety before travelling and often encounter security checkpoints around the city.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: But she says their experience on the ground is generally positive.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Lido beach is one of the most popular places for people to relax in Mogadishu "What they heard from the news and everywhere else is not the same as what they see in the country," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Although some question whether Mogadishu is safe enough for a young woman to be working as a tour guide, Sucdi is determined to continue.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She wants visitors to experience a Somalia that is rarely seen.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I would want them to see the beautiful, welcoming side of Mogadishu, and not the side that they heard from the media, which is explosions and bombs," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Somalia has Africa's longest mainland coastline, stretching more than 3,000km (1,860 miles) along the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Its beaches and sand dunes sit alongside historic coastal cities such as Mogadishu, whose culture reflects centuries of Indian Ocean trade.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Mogadishu is a growing commercial hub For some tourists, that contrast between the country's reputation and what they experience can be striking.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: American travel content creator Chris Reese, who goes by the name Authentic Travelling, has visited Mogadishu twice.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: His first trip, almost a year ago, was a solo visit.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: He enjoyed it so much that he decided to return with a group of friends, who had seen videos of his visit on social media.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I had such a positive experience - I really enjoyed seeing the country for the first time - that I opted to bring back a group of my friends," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: What stands out for Chris is the city's coastal setting, its food and atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "It is such a beautiful tropical place.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: I love the vibe, the weather and the food," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: The sand dunes near Mogadishu remind some visitors of the Sahara Desert During the group's visit, they enjoy lunch overlooking the Indian Ocean before heading out to explore the beaches and sand dunes.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "The desert is beautiful and picturesque.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: It is also amazing that it's barely a 30-minute drive from Mogadishu," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Before his first trip, Chris says, much of what he knew about Somalia came from international news coverage.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "If you only read the news reports about Somalia, you would be scared to visit.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: And honestly, that's what I saw in the media before I came, mostly negative headlines." But visiting the country challenged those perceptions.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "Coming here, on my very first trip, showed me that there is so much more to this country than what is shown in the headlines," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Romanian Mihaela Patap says she prefers to visit new countries without preconceived ideas Mihaela Patap, from Romania, loves Somalia's natural beauty.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Although she has spent only a few hours in Mogadishu, she has already visited the sand dunes and taken in the Indian Ocean coastline.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "The desert was so beautiful to see.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: I have also enjoyed the beach, and the ocean.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: It is inspiring," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Having travelled to Somalia from neighbouring Ethiopia, she says she has been struck by the people's friendliness.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I don't see anything dangerous.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: I feel safe and the people are warm," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: An experienced traveller, Mihaela says she prefers to visit new countries without having preconceived ideas.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I travel the world to see new places, to see countries, to see the differences.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: I don't take a picture in my mind to compare the reality with.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: I'm just expecting the new to come to me," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: She hopes to share her experience and encourage others to visit Somalia.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: "I'm going to post my pictures and say good things about what I'm experiencing.

sentences.text: I'm going to promote it," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: For Sucdi, that potential is personal.
sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Joseph Kabila was a commander in the rebel alliance that brought his father to power in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1997, went on to succeed him as president and now, at the age of 55, he is a rebel leader once again.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: In an even stranger twist, the man he has sworn to topple is the very man he handed power to after 18 years at the helm, and with whom he had formed a coalition government after stepping down.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: While one of the rebel groups he had fought against as president is part of his new alliance.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: His career reflects the ever-shifting nature of politics in DR Congo, where alliances are ephemeral, with the use of force a constant threat.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: When Kabila was named leader of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), earlier this month, it confirmed what many Congolese had long believed – that the former president was working with the M23 rebels, who last year seized much of eastern DR Congo, including the region's main cities of Goma and Bukavu.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: Nevertheless, the confirmation sent shockwaves through DR Congo – a vast country two-thirds the size of western Europe, with huge deposits of gold, diamonds and even more importantly minerals used to make everything from the mobile phones to batteries for electric vehicles.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: For Kabila, the alliance offers a possible route back to the power he had lost.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: For the M23 rebels, his involvement brings the experience and networks of a former head of state to a movement whose military advances have yet to translate into broad national legitimacy.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: But it is far from certain that they can achieve their stated goal of ousting President Félix Tshisekedi.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: Kabila (left) and President Tshisekedi entered a political coalition in 2019 Policy analyst Henry-Pacifique Mayala told the BBC that Kabila had been left with few options for regaining political influence.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: "He actually was left with no other choice," he said.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: Facing a death sentence after being convicted in absentia of treason, as well as US sanctions over his alleged support for the M23, Kabila may have sought assurances that the partnership could serve his interests, Mayala suggested.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: "I'm not sure that he is making this huge leap in the dark without having received considerable assurance," Mayala said, adding that the M23's military strength could give Kabila greater leverage in any future negotiations with the Congolese government.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: Kabila's involvement also raises questions about whether the conflict could spread beyond the east.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: The M23's territorial gains have been concentrated in the country's eastern provinces, some 1,500km (1,000 miles) from the capital, Kinshasa.

sentences.text: Kabila's political networks could give the rebellion a broader reach, but that does not necessarily mean it has the capacity to extend its military campaign across the country.

sentences.text: And it is not clear how far Kabila's national reach extends.

sentences.text: His father's rebel group actually walked across the country to Kinshasa, also starting in the east, over a period of seven months, before eventually seizing power in May 1996 and ousting long-time ruler Mobutu Sese Seko, who had governed the country as his own personal property for more than 30 years.

sentences.text: There is little suggestion that Joseph Kabila's FRN would try to repeat that feat but earlier this week, he likened Tshisekedi to Mobutu.

sentences.text: In April, Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon became the first female blind sambist in the world to win a gold medal at a major international tournament Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon only took up sambo this year, but the Nigerian has already secured her place in the history of the martial art.

sentences.text: The sport shares strong roots with judo and wrestling, combining techniques such as hip and leg throws to take opponents to the mat, where they can be pinned.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: Competing at the 2026 World Sambo Cup in Armenia, Suleimon defeated Uzbekistan's Charos Ortikova in the final of the women's 54kg category to claim victory on her international debut.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: It was the first time that women with visual impairments had been included at the competition.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: "This is my first time in sambo and God crowned my efforts." Suleimon's achievement was part of a breakthrough moment for African women in the sport.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: She and compatriot Elizabeth Aseso, who competed in the 59kg category, were among the pioneering sambists representing the continent in Yerevan.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: For Suleimon, her gold medal is a reward for the hard work over many years which has seen her move from athletics to judo and now to the top of the international sambo podium.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.text: "I really benefit a lot from sports and, despite my blindness, I achieve a lot," she said.
sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa

sentences.article_title: She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa
